previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, depression, anxiety, and a history of venous thrombosis and C. difficile, was readmitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with an acute flare of her chronic pancreatitis. She had difficulty with IV access, requiring a midline catheter placement after failed PICC attempts. She was managed with IV fluids, analgesics, and antiemetics, then transitioned to oral tramadol and a regular diet as her symptoms improved. Her lipase was normal, and stool testing ruled out C. difficile. Hypertension was managed with lisinopril and the addition of amlodipine. She remained mentally stable, tolerated discharge on a regular diet, and was sent home with all home medications and follow-up instructions.

Pt states that she was in her usual state of health until 5 days

describes that this is her usual pancreatitis pain. 
Subsequently, she developed nausea with nonbloody nonbilious

despite her home IM phenergen so she presented to the ED for 
further evaluation.

tox + TCA, urine tox + opiates, otherwise negative. Persistent 
abdominal pain and tenderness on exam, unable to tolerate PO. 
She was treated with medication as per ED protocol, receiving a 
total of 2mg IV Ativan, 6mg IV diluadid, 50mg promethazine, 
toradol 30mg and 2L of LR. She was admitted to medicine for

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman whose PMH includes chronic 
pancreatitis with frequent hospital admissions for acute 
exacerbations, most recently at ___ from ___, c diff 
colitis, as well as major depression with previous suicide 
attempts who presented with abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting 
concerning for acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis.
 
# Acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis: Pt reported on 
admission that symptoms were consistent with previous 
exacerbations. She was in severe abdominal pain with associated 
nausea, vomiting and inability to tolerate PO intake. Work-up 
revealed lipase of 43 but was otherwise unremarkable. Clinical 
picture was not concerning for infectious process. Urine and 
serum toxicology screen were performed that was positive for 
TCAs and opiates, both of which could be expected based on her 
medication list. She stated that her underlying pancreatitis is 
related to CF gene mutation. She denied alcohol use and is 
status post cholecystectomy. The etiology of current 
exacerbation and recent increase in frequency of exacerbations 
over the last several months remains unclear. After arrival she 
was initiated on the protocol that had been designed by her 
primary outpatient team including rehydration with IVF, pain 
control with toradol and dilaudid, and antiemetic regimen of 
promethazine and lorazepam (see note in OMR from ___ for full 
details). Her abdominal pain gradually improved over the next 
several days although remained unable to tolerate significant 
oral intake. After she was consistently tolerating a diet she 
was transitioned to oral medication regimen and was ready for 
discharge shortly thereafter.   
 
# HTN: SBP was elevated to 180 while in the ED. This was most 
likely due to missed doses of medication as well as pain and 
anxiety. Her SBP improved but remained mildly elevated after 
restarting home medication regimen of lisinopril and amlodipine. 
Her amlodipine dose was uptitrated from 5mg to 10mg daily prior 
to discharge. She will need continued BP monitoring as an 
outpatient with further medication uptitration as needed. 

# GERD: IV pantoprazole was substituted for home omeprazole 
while unable to tolerate PO. She was transitioned back to home 
regimen prior to discharge. 

# Depression: Pt reported that her mood remained at baseline. 
Her home seroquel and amitriptyline were continued. 

# Headaches: Home fioricet was continued as needed.

- Discharged on home medication regimen
- Increased amlodipine from 5mg daily to 10mg daily due to 
elevated SBPs. Please recheck BP as outpatient and titrate meds
